commands_run: clan patch-data test-sandbox/happy/heavy/h2-clan-rep5/work/doc.clan test-sandbox/happy/heavy/h2-clan-rep5/work/hop11-legal.json --agent 11-legal-reviewer --action "added 11-legal-reviewer findings" --rationale "NetSuite connector creates unaddressed GDPR sub-processor chain; liability cap below GDPR fine exposure; DPA negotiation required before contract signature"

errors.what: clan patch-data failed with /tmp/h2-r5-hop11.json — Windows resolves /tmp to AppData/Local/Temp, but Write tool wrote to Linux-style /tmp which is not the same path clan (native Windows binary) sees
errors.recovered_by: Wrote JSON to project-local path test-sandbox/happy/heavy/h2-clan-rep5/work/hop11-legal.json and re-ran patch-data with that path; succeeded

problems_and_friction: The /tmp path mismatch on Windows (Write tool uses POSIX /tmp; clan binary resolves to AppData/Local/Temp) caused one failed patch attempt. Workaround was to use a project-relative path. Prior analysts left solid gdpr_* fields which informed but did not duplicate legal findings — chain design worked well here.
context_understood: Brightline Logistics (40 seats, EU-based) evaluating Zoho CRM as recommended vendor at EUR18,240/yr; legal review focuses on GDPR DPA adequacy, liability gap, and sub-processor chain risk introduced by the third-party NetSuite connector.
